quest.title: For All Children Who Long for Life
quest.description: Now, only the final enemy awaits vanquishing. Continue forward. Never, ever, stop moving forward.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

talks.objective: Go to the deepest part of the cave

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Now that we have destroyed Marana's Avatar, peace should be restored in the forest. Well, I said "we," but it was mostly due to your efforts and courage. Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: It was really thanks to the garland and everyone's support...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They gave me the courage to keep going.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Each flower is connected with the heart of an Aranara. One could even say that a garland of these flowers woven together can form the door to "Mahavana{RUBY#[S]the Aranara universe}ranapna."

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: As long as it connects us, we can support you when you are in need, lend you strength to conquer nightmares, help you through dark days, and fill the void in your heart.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: There are those who no longer dream and thus can no longer see us, those who have accepted fate and stopped searching for the way forward, and those who wallow in fear and pain. Their hearts have hardened, unable to get help from these flowers.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #It's because Nara {NICKNAME} is kind and honest, and because Nara {NICKNAME} is Nara {NICKNAME}, that the garland could serve its purpose.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is Aranara's friend. We won't leave our friend alone to fight Marana and eliminate all evil for a brighter and purer world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME} is Paimon's best friend, so of course {F#she's}{M#he's} the best person ever! Anyway, Paimon guesses this Withering business has been settled once and for all then, right?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Marana should fall into slumber now that its avatar has been destroyed. But in a matter of decades, perhaps centuries, it will wake up again.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: It's because Marana's memory has been left in Sarva. Unless that can be completely removed, the memory of "death" that dwells in all things will eventually bring it back again.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #...But this will take a long time. I believe that by then there will once again come someone as golden as the sun, just like Nara {NICKNAME} and Nara Varuna, so I wouldn't worry about it.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Today's forest has a bright future ahead. As long as what remains of Marana is cleared, the children of the forest will be able to enjoy abundant sunshine and rain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Anyway, now that Marana's Avatar is destroyed, the next step is to plant a new Ashvattha Tree for the Bija, right?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes. Please wait here for a moment while I fetch Arana.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Arana... Right, we've gotta use Arana's memories to produce the Bija...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But isn't Arana around Vimara Village? How are we gonna...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And there Arama goes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa!

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, Arana sensed your battle against Marana's Avatar. You and Arama are very brave.

choices.text: How did you come all the way here in just a second...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I've received Aramuhukunda's memories. Through them, I learned how to use Sarva to travel through the forest in a flash. This particular Ararakalari is called "teleportation."

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Arama is amazing. Aramuhukunda must be so glad that you were the one receiving his memory. Arana hasn't teleported in a long, long time either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Next, we need to plant a new Ashvattha Tree, right? Paimon remembers that Arama talked about some seed thingy...

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: Seeds know that they have to grow into big trees and bear lots of big fruits... Thank you, Arama.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: No problem. I will grow into a new Ashvattha Tree, bear the Bija using your memories and dreams, and use my roots to reconnect the corroded bridges between dreams.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. What are you guys talking about?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Having absorbed the memories and energies of Aramuhukunda, the Ashvattha Tree, and the Vasoma Fruits, I have now become the strongest "seed" in the forest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Paimon doesn't understand...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I was planning to build up my memories with my own eyes and body for several decades or centuries, and then embrace the land again to grow into a beautiful Vasara Tree.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have had the honor to heal the forest by destroying Marana's Avatar, or become the king of the Vasara Trees by collecting all these precious memories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so... the Vasara Trees in Ashvattha's Concourses were all once Aranara?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, they were once Araji, Arayama, and Aramaha. The Vasoma Fruits are their memories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if you turn into a tree, Arama, you would lose the ability to run, talk, and sing...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Though I did not spend many days as a seed, the days I spent with you are ten times, no, hundreds of times more precious than the days I spent before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not fair... Paimon still has plans to hang out with you...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #I see... I understand, Paimon. Nara {NICKNAME} and you are my friends. This will never change...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: With all these memories and energies I've received, I'm now able to see many scenes and stories in Sarva. Let me tell you one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Hidden in the golden sandstorm, the eternal oasis was devoid of life. The oldest ruler of all plants, whom no Aranara had had the pleasure of meeting, lay dormant in the sand.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The vegetation that once covered it had all died and been reduced to grains of sand. Just as Marana whispered: All good things must vanish.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: But you should know that as dark as night is, the stars still shine and the sun will still rise. Death longs to dominate all, but life will not fade.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Just like the yellow leaves that fall down shall nourish Cuihua Trees, their fruits shall sustain Sumpter Beasts, foxes, and forest boars, while they shall feed Rishboland Tigers in turn. And so, the forest always teems with life.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Once, the land was polluted with toxic blood. Like Nara, Aranara too thought that was the end of the world, but now even the memory of it is gone. The forest is even more luxuriant than it was in the time of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: In the end, all that remains is beautiful. Those who part will come to meet again in Sarva.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: One day, our dreams and memories will intertwine and blossom on the numberless branches in Sarva. Wouldn't that be great?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon understands, but...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... Alright. Paimon understands! You're the best seed, Arama! You'll definitely grow into a great and beautiful tree!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #And... and even when you've turned into a tree, please don't forget Paimon and {NICKNAME}, and the adventures we had together!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. It's been a great pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Arana, I promise I will turn your memories into the most beautiful and robust Bija.

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: I believe you, Arama.

choices.text: Wait. What are you guys talking about?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I'm the seed for the new Ashvattha Tree. Having absorbed the memories and energies of Aramuhukunda, the Ashvattha Tree, and the Vasoma Fruits, I have now become the strongest "seed" in the forest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That was a close call... Thankfully, {NICKNAME} was wearing that garland! It's even more amazing than Paimon thought!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: This is where the last war ended. We... They crushed Marana's Avatar and imprisoned it here with the four seals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks scary... So is Marana's Avatar in there?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Marana has corroded the Vasara Tree that was meant to grow atop it and has gained possession of its bodily form. If left unchecked, it'll eventually eat away at all life on this earth.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Since it's not at its full strength yet, now would be the best time to destroy its avatar. With it defeated, we should be able to obtain the Bija.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Come, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, let's get going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're speaking normally again, Arama...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You claim the Bija.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We finally got it. The precious Bija...

choices.text: We've certainly come a long way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Now all we need to do is to give it to Rana, right?

response.speaker: Arana
response.text: ...Who are you?

response.text: Yes. May we never meet again, Marana. Many tiny Marana remain in the forest, but we've defeated the greatest one.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I can sense that all memories about Marana in Sarva have been completely erased. In this case, even the memory and fear of "death" that dwells in all things cannot bring it back ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arama...

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: Arama has grown into the new Ashvattha Tree. It's small now, but the roots are deep and strong. After many, many moons, it will surely grow to be big and beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arana, you once said that memories and dreams are Aranara's source of strength. If you give those memories up, you'll forget Rana, won't you? And the children of Vimara Village too...

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: Yes. But friends are more precious than memories. You can always make up for lost memories, but not a lost friend.

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: I want to help Narana. She has the same name as Arana. She is Arana's friend.

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: And even if Arana doesn't remember, you will. As long as you remember, your memory will one day grow into a ripe and robust fruit...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon understands...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What should we do?

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: #Arana has taught you the Rhythm of the Great Dream. Do you still remember it, Nara {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: Just play this song to Arana and Arama.

talks.objective: Play the Rhythm of the Great Dream

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, please make it quick. The Ararakalari that Arana left with Narana won't last long.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Arana
dialogues.text: Yes. I'll be fine.
